title: Small step errors accumulate
hook: Which method avoids compounding this repeated bias?

knows: Everyday objects have sizes, positions and amounts
doesNotKnow: A biased step repeated from the previous mark adds its error each time. Measuring each chosen position from one origin avoids that particular accumulation, though the measuring tool can still have its own errors.

recall.question: Each 10 cm step you mark comes out 0.3 cm long. How far off is the 6th mark when you step from the last mark each time, and when you measure each one from the start?
recall.why: Stepping from the last mark adds the bias every time: 6 × 0.3 = 1.8 cm. Reading each position from one origin keeps a single 0.3 cm error. The bias is hypothetical.
